Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anyway adverb

in any case, whatever happens

also anyhow, in any case, be that as it may, however that may be, whatever happens, regardless, regardless of what happens, irrespective, at any rate

classical

Liv. praef. 3: utcumque erit, juvābit tamen

utcumque

adverb; utcumque est (erit), however that is (will be)

however it is, whatever happens

The main clause usually carries tamen, “all the same” (see however).

Other words

  • utut est (utut haec sunt) — however that may be

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 531: sed utut haec sunt, tamen hoc faciam; Plaut. Merc. 558: vērum hercle postrēmō, utut est, nōn ībō tamen

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: mostly ante-classical))

  • utique — in any case, by all means

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.4.1: quō diē veniēs, utique cum tuīs apud mē sīs; Traupman 106: at any rate, utique

    In Cicero mostly in the letters (Lewis & Short; see also at least).

Examples

  • Sed utut haec sunt, tamen hoc faciam.

    But however that may be, this is what I’ll do anyway.Ter. Ph. 531

  • quō diē veniēs, utique cum tuīs apud mē sīs

    whichever day you come, stay with me in any case, with your familyCic. Att. 4.4.1

See also anyway, however, at least.
